title: Ang biyaheng hindi malilimutan: travel, mishaps, narration
objectives: Report misfortunes with the adversative na--an: nawalan, naubusan, nasiraan, naiwanan
Chain events with pag-/pagka- clauses: right after arriving, upon waking
Pace a story with bigla, kaagad, unti-unti, sa wakas, buti na lang
Tell an extended past-tense travel story from start to finish

grammar.title: When bad things happen to you: the adversative na--an
grammar.explanation:
Tagalog has a dedicated pattern for misfortunes that befall you: na- + root + -an, with the victim as the ang-phrase and the thing lost or affected as a ng-phrase.

Nawalan ako ng wallet — I lost my wallet (more literally: I was bereft of a wallet). Compare Unit 2's nawala ang wallet ko, which spotlights the wallet; nawalan ako spotlights you as the affected person — the natural choice when the story is about your bad day. Naubusan kami ng gasolina — we ran out of gas. Nasiraan sila ng kotse sa daan — their car broke down on them on the road. Naiwanan ako ng bus — the bus left me behind (compare naiwan ko ang payong, where you left the umbrella).

Aspect: nawalan / nawawalan / mawawalan, naubusan / nauubusan / mauubusan, and so on. The same shape covers being caught by weather and events: naulanan kami — we got rained on; naabutan kami ng trapiko — we got caught in traffic (literally 'traffic caught up with us'). This pattern plus Unit 2's accidental na- verbs gives you the full vocabulary of things going wrong — which is to say, the full vocabulary of a memorable trip.

examples.tl: Nawalan ako ng cellphone sa terminal.
examples.en: I lost my cellphone at the terminal.

examples.tl: Naubusan kami ng gasolina sa gitna ng bundok.
examples.en: We ran out of gas in the middle of the mountains.

examples.tl: Nasiraan ng bangka ang mga mangingisda kahapon.
examples.en: The fishermen's boat broke down on them yesterday.

examples.tl: Muntik na kaming maiwanan ng huling biyahe.
examples.en: We almost got left behind by the last trip.

examples.tl: Naulanan kami habang naghihintay ng traysikel.
examples.en: We got rained on while waiting for a tricycle.

examples.tl: Mauubusan tayo ng tiket kung hindi tayo bibili ngayon.
examples.en: We'll run out of tickets if we don't buy now.

grammar.title: Right after: pag- and pagka- clauses
grammar.explanation:
You know pagkatapos + verb noun for 'after'. Narration has a tighter, more vivid tool: pag- or pagka- attached straight to the verb root, with the doer as a ng-phrase or possessive. Pagdating ko sa hotel, natulog agad ako — as soon as I arrived at the hotel, I slept right away. Pag-uwi namin, kakain tayo sa labas — when we get home, we'll eat out.

Pag- + root is the everyday form: pagdating (upon arriving), pag-alis (upon leaving), paggising (upon waking), pagbaba (upon getting off). Pagka- adds a 'right after completing' flavor: pagkakain namin, umalis kami — right after we ate, we left; pagkagising ko, tumawag agad ako sa ospital. In practice they overlap, and pagka- also doubles in forms like pagkatapos, which you already own.

These clauses are the skeleton of Tagalog storytelling: each one hands the timeline to the next event without a heavy conjunction. Pagbaba ko ng bus, naramdaman kong wala ang bag ko — the moment I got off the bus, I felt that my bag was gone. Notice there's no tense marking inside the pag- clause; the main verb carries the aspect, so the same pag-uwi ko works for past and future stories alike.

examples.tl: Pagdating namin sa isla, kumain agad kami ng tanghalian.
examples.en: As soon as we arrived on the island, we ate lunch right away.

examples.tl: Paggising ko kinabukasan, umuulan na nang malakas.
examples.en: When I woke up the next day, it was already raining hard.

examples.tl: Pagkakain namin, naglakad kami papunta sa tabing-dagat.
examples.en: Right after we ate, we walked toward the beach.

examples.tl: Pagbaba mo sa terminal, tumawag ka agad sa akin.
examples.en: The moment you get off at the terminal, call me right away.

examples.tl: Pag-alis ng bangka, biglang lumakas ang hangin.
examples.en: As the boat left, the wind suddenly picked up.

grammar.title: Pacing a story: bigla, kaagad, unti-unti, sa wakas
grammar.explanation:
A good story controls speed. Tagalog's pacing words:

Bigla — suddenly. As an adverb it takes the linker: biglang bumuhos ang ulan — the rain suddenly poured. Also bigla na lang — 'just out of nowhere': Bigla na lang siyang umiyak. Kaagad / agad — immediately, right away: Tumawag agad kami sa talyer. Unti-unti — little by little: Unti-unting humupa ang ulan — the rain gradually eased. Mamaya-maya — after a while: Mamaya-maya, may dumating na traysikel. Sa wakas — finally, at last: Sa wakas, nakarating din kami. Habang-narration you already do; add sa kasamaang-palad — unfortunately — and its hero twin buti na lang — luckily / good thing: Buti na lang, may dalang extrang gasolina si Kuya.

A typical mishap story runs: setup in the incompleted aspect (Maganda ang panahon, kumakanta pa kami sa bangka...), then bigla flips it (biglang kumulog), a chain of completed verbs races through the crisis (naubusan pa kami ng gasolina, nawalan ng signal ang cellphone), buti na lang turns the tide, and sa wakas lands the ending. Practice this arc; it's the shape of every Filipino travel story told over dinner.

examples.tl: Biglang namatay ang makina ng bangka sa gitna ng dagat.
examples.en: The boat's engine suddenly died in the middle of the sea.

examples.tl: Bumaba agad kami nang huminto ang bus.
examples.en: We got off immediately when the bus stopped.

examples.tl: Unti-unting lumiwanag ang langit pagkatapos ng bagyo.
examples.en: The sky gradually brightened after the storm.

examples.tl: Sa kasamaang-palad, sarado na ang huling gasolinahan.
examples.en: Unfortunately, the last gas station was already closed.

examples.tl: Buti na lang, may nakasalubong kaming traysikel.
examples.en: Luckily, we came across a tricycle.

examples.tl: Sa wakas, nakarating din kami sa hotel bago maghatinggabi.
examples.en: Finally, we reached the hotel before midnight.

vocab.note: nawalan, nawawalan, mawawalan; thing lost takes ng

example.tl: Nawalan siya ng pasaporte sa paliparan.
example.en: He lost his passport at the airport.

example.tl: Naubusan kami ng pera sa huling araw ng bakasyon.
example.en: We ran out of money on the last day of the vacation.

vocab.en: to have one's (vehicle, appliance) break down

example.tl: Nasiraan kami ng kotse sa may tulay.
example.en: Our car broke down on us near the bridge.

vocab.en: to be left behind by (a ride)
vocab.note: naiwanan, naiiwanan, maiiwanan; compare naiwan (you left a thing)

example.tl: Naiwanan kami ng barko dahil na-late kami ng limang minuto.
example.en: The ship left us behind because we were five minutes late.

example.tl: Naligaw kami sa maliliit na kalye ng lumang bayan.
example.en: We got lost in the little streets of the old town.

vocab.en: to be caught by; to catch (in time)
vocab.note: naabutan, naaabutan, maaabutan; naabutan kami ng ulan = the rain caught us

example.tl: Buti na lang, naabutan pa namin ang huling biyahe.
example.en: Luckily, we still caught the last trip.

vocab.note: huling biyahe = last trip of the day

example.tl: Anim na oras ang biyahe papuntang Baguio.
example.en: The trip to Baguio is six hours.

example.tl: Bumiyahe kami nang gabi para makatipid sa oras.
example.en: We traveled at night to save time.

example.tl: Ilagay mo ang pasaporte sa bulsang may zipper.
example.en: Put the passport in the zippered pocket.

example.tl: Ang bigat ng maleta mo — ano ang laman nito?
example.en: Your suitcase is so heavy — what's in it?

vocab.note: the English loan 'airport' is also common

example.tl: Dapat nasa paliparan ka tatlong oras bago ang alis.
example.en: You should be at the airport three hours before departure.

example.tl: Puno ng tao ang terminal tuwing Semana Santa.
example.en: The terminal is packed with people every Holy Week.

example.tl: Sumakay kami ng maliit na bangka papunta sa isla.
example.en: We rode a small boat to the island.

example.tl: Magkano na ang gasolina kada litro ngayon?
example.en: How much is gasoline per liter now?

example.tl: Huminto tayo sa susunod na gasolinahan.
example.en: Let's stop at the next gas station.

example.tl: Pumutok ang gulong namin sa highway.
example.en: Our tire blew out on the highway.

example.tl: Walang signal, kaya binuksan namin ang lumang mapa.
example.en: There was no signal, so we opened the old map.

example.tl: May aksidente sa kanto kaya mabagal ang daloy ng mga sasakyan.
example.en: There was an accident at the corner, so traffic is moving slowly.

example.tl: Magkano ang pamasahe hanggang sa bayan?
example.en: How much is the fare to town?

vocab.note: with linker: biglang tumakbo; bigla na lang = out of nowhere

example.tl: Biglang bumuhos ang ulan habang naglalakad kami.
example.en: The rain suddenly poured while we were walking.

vocab.note: shortened to agad; agad-agad = at once

example.tl: Pagdating namin, nagpahinga kaagad ang mga bata.
example.en: As soon as we arrived, the kids rested right away.

example.tl: Unti-unting bumalik ang kuryente sa buong bayan.
example.en: Electricity gradually came back to the whole town.

example.tl: Sa wakas, nakita rin namin ang hinahanap na resort.
example.en: At last, we found the resort we were looking for.

example.tl: Sa kasamaang-palad, kanselado ang lahat ng biyahe dahil sa bagyo.
example.en: Unfortunately, all trips were canceled because of the typhoon.

example.tl: Buti na lang, nagdala ako ng extrang damit.
example.en: Good thing I brought extra clothes.

example.tl: Mamaya-maya, dumating din ang hinihintay naming jeep.
example.en: After a while, the jeepney we were waiting for finally came.

vocab.note: pag-uwi ko = when I get/got home

example.tl: Pag-uwi namin, ikinuwento namin agad ang lahat kay Nanay.
example.en: When we got home, we immediately told Mom everything.

example.tl: Naglakad kami sa tabing-dagat habang lumulubog ang araw.
example.en: We walked along the seaside while the sun was setting.

dialogue.title: Ang kuwento ng biyahe
dialogue.context: Back at work, Paolo tells Dina about his island trip that went spectacularly wrong.

lines.speaker: Dina
lines.tl: Kumusta ang bakasyon mo sa isla? Nakita ko ang mga litrato — ang ganda!
lines.en: How was your island vacation? I saw the photos — beautiful!

lines.speaker: Paolo
lines.tl: Maganda nga, pero muntik na kaming hindi makarating. Mahaba ang kuwento.
lines.en: Beautiful indeed, but we almost didn't make it. It's a long story.

lines.speaker: Dina
lines.tl: Ikuwento mo nga! Bakante pa naman ako ng sampung minuto.
lines.en: Do tell! I'm still free for ten minutes anyway.

lines.speaker: Paolo
lines.tl: Pagdating namin sa terminal, nalaman naming naiwanan na kami ng unang barko.
lines.en: When we got to the terminal, we found out the first ship had already left us behind.

lines.speaker: Dina
lines.en: Oh no! Why were you late?

lines.speaker: Paolo
lines.tl: Nasiraan kami ng kotse sa daan. Flat pa ang gulong, tapos naubusan kami ng gasolina!
lines.en: The car broke down on us on the way. A flat tire, and then we ran out of gas!

lines.speaker: Dina
lines.en: One thing after another! How did you get going?

lines.speaker: Paolo
lines.tl: Buti na lang, may dumaang traysikel. Bumili agad si Marco ng gasolina sa bayan.
lines.en: Luckily, a tricycle passed by. Marco immediately bought gas in town.

lines.speaker: Dina
lines.tl: Tapos, naabutan pa ba ninyo ang ibang biyahe?
lines.en: And then, did you still catch another trip?

lines.speaker: Paolo
lines.tl: Oo, ang huling bangka ng hapon. Pero pag-alis namin, biglang lumakas ang alon!
lines.en: Yes, the last boat of the afternoon. But as we left, the waves suddenly got strong!

lines.speaker: Dina
lines.tl: Diyos ko. Buti hindi kayo naulanan man lang?
lines.en: My goodness. Good thing you didn't even get rained on?

lines.speaker: Paolo
lines.tl: Naulanan din! Pero sa wakas, nakarating kami — basang-basa, gutom, pero masaya.
lines.en: We got rained on too! But at last we arrived — soaking wet, hungry, but happy.

reading.title: Dalawang araw sa isla
reading.tl:
Noong isang buwan, bumiyahe kami ng tatlong kaibigan ko papunta sa isang isla sa Quezon. Maaga kaming umalis, pero sa kasamaang-palad, naabutan pa rin kami ng trapiko dahil may aksidente. Pagdating namin sa terminal, alas-dose na — naiwanan na kami ng unang bangka.

Habang naghihintay ng susunod na biyahe, nawalan pa ako ng tsinelas: naanod ito habang naglalaro kami. Mamaya-maya, dumating din ang bangka. Pag-alis namin, kalmado ang dagat, pero unti-unting dumilim ang langit. Biglang bumuhos ang ulan, at basang-basa kami pagdating sa isla.

Buti na lang, mabait ang pamilyang may-ari ng tinutuluyan namin. Pinahiram nila kami ng tuyong damit at pinainom ng mainit na salabat. Kinabukasan, pagkagising ko, maaraw na: naglangoy kami at nag-ihaw ng isda sa tabing-dagat. Pag-uwi namin, sabi ng mga kaibigan ko, babalik daw kami sa susunod na taon. Sang-ayon ako — pero aalis kami nang mas maaga, at magdadala ako ng dalawang pares ng tsinelas.
reading.en:
Last month, three friends and I traveled to an island in Quezon. We left early, but unfortunately we still got caught in traffic because of an accident. When we reached the terminal, it was already noon — the first boat had left without us.

While waiting for the next trip, I also lost my flip-flops: they were carried off by the water while we were playing. After a while, the boat finally came. When we set off, the sea was calm, but the sky gradually darkened. Suddenly the rain poured down, and we were soaked when we reached the island.

Luckily, the family who owned the place we were staying at was kind. They lent us dry clothes and gave us hot ginger tea to drink. The next day, when I woke up, it was sunny: we swam and grilled fish by the seaside. On our way home, my friends said we'd come back next year. I agree — but we'll leave earlier, and I'm bringing two pairs of flip-flops.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'We ran out of gas'?
exercises.explain: The adversative na--an puts the victims in focus: naubusan kami ng gasolina. Choice 3 means we deliberately used it all up; choice 4 is future.

exercises.prompt: What is the difference between 'naiwan ko ang bag' and 'naiwanan ako ng bus'?
choices: The first: I left the bag behind; the second: the bus left me behind
The first is future, the second past
The first is polite, the second rude
exercises.explain: Naiwan (ma-) = you accidentally left a thing; naiwanan (na--an) = something (the bus) left YOU — the adversative flips who is affected.

exercises.prompt: ___ ako ng wallet sa jeep kahapon, kaya walang-wala ako ngayon. (I lost my wallet — victim in focus)
exercises.explain: Nawalan ako ng wallet spotlights you as the person deprived; nawala ang wallet ko would spotlight the wallet.

exercises.prompt: ___ ko sa hotel, natulog agad ako. (As soon as I arrived at the hotel...)
exercises.explain: Pag- + root + possessor builds a 'right after' clause: pagdating ko = upon my arriving.

exercises.prompt: Pick the natural pacing for a mishap: 'Kalmado ang dagat. ___ lumakas ang hangin.'
exercises.explain: The sudden turn in a story is biglang + verb: the wind suddenly picked up. Unti-unti would be a slow change.

exercises.tl: Nasiraan kami ng kotse sa daan, pero buti na lang may malapit na talyer.
choices: They crashed the car into a shop
Their car broke down, but luckily there was a repair shop nearby
They ran out of gas far from any shop
The repair shop was closed when their car broke down
exercises.explain: Nasiraan kami ng kotse = the car broke down on us; buti na lang = luckily; talyer = auto repair shop (Unit 3).

exercises.prompt: We got rained on while waiting for the bus.
exercises.answer: Naulanan kami habang naghihintay ng bus.
accept: Naulanan kami habang naghihintay ng bus
Naulanan kami habang naghihintay kami ng bus
Inulan kami habang naghihintay ng bus
exercises.explain: Being caught by rain is the adversative naulanan; habang + incompleted verb sets the simultaneous background.

exercises.prompt: Pagbaba ko ng bus, naramdaman kong wala na ang telepono ko.
exercises.answer: The moment I got off the bus, I felt that my phone was gone.
accept: The moment I got off the bus, I felt that my phone was gone
As soon as I got off the bus I felt my phone was gone
When I got off the bus, I realized my phone was missing
exercises.explain: Pagbaba ko = upon my getting off; naramdaman kong + clause = I felt that...; wala na = gone already.

exercises.prompt: Sa ___ , nakarating din kami sa resort bago gumabi. (Finally, we made it...)
exercises.explain: Sa wakas caps a story after difficulties: 'at last'. Nakarating (maka-) adds the 'managed to' flavor.

exercises.prompt: Order the story naturally: (a) Biglang bumuhos ang ulan. (b) Maganda ang panahon nang umalis kami. (c) Buti na lang may dala kaming payong. (d) Sa wakas, nakarating kami nang tuyo.
exercises.explain: Setup (b: nice weather), sudden turn (a: bigla), rescue (c: buti na lang), resolution (d: sa wakas) — the standard mishap arc.

exercises.tl: Muntik na kaming maiwanan ng huling biyahe kasi naligaw kami papunta sa terminal.
choices: They missed the last trip because they got lost
They almost got left behind by the last trip because they got lost on the way to the terminal
They left the terminal early to avoid getting lost
The last trip was canceled because of an accident
exercises.explain: Muntik na (Unit 2) = almost; maiwanan = be left behind; naligaw kami = we got lost. Disaster narrowly avoided.

exercises.prompt: Right after we ate, we walked to the seaside.
exercises.answer: Pagkakain namin, naglakad kami papunta sa tabing-dagat.
accept: Pagkakain namin, naglakad kami papunta sa tabing-dagat
Pagkatapos naming kumain, naglakad kami papunta sa tabing-dagat
Pagkakain namin naglakad kami sa tabing-dagat
exercises.explain: Pagka- + kain + namin = right after our eating; papunta sa marks the direction of the walk.
